title: openai-chat-completions-parity: roles, stop/logprobs, streaming, function-calls, structured output
author: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement parity for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics across: explicit role handling, 'stop' token behavior, logprobs export, streaming stability, function/tool calling behavior, and consistent structured-output formatting. Motivation: the OpenAI compatibility layer currently has subtle differences in message role normalization, stop sequence handling during streaming, and function call/event emission. These differences have caused downstream parsing regressions and customer support tickets (linked ENG-1423). This PR centralizes the compatibility contract and adds conformance tests.

What changed (high-level):
- API layer: normalize incoming chat messages to OpenAI semantics (roles: system/user/assistant/tool) and validate unknown roles with a warning rather than hard error to preserve existing behavior for SDKs.
- Stop sequences: implement streaming-aware stop detection that ensures tokens that complete a stop sequence are emitted in the same event ordering as OpenAI (no partial token truncation in intermediate chunks). We now support multiple stop sequences and prioritize earliest match.
- Logprobs: expose token-level logprobs in non-streaming and streaming “final” payloads. Streaming partial logprobs are omitted until final chunk to avoid churn; final event includes aggregated token-level logprobs in the same array ordering as tokens.
- Function/tool calling: respect function call hints from OpenAI-style messages (name + arguments) and emit 'tool.call' events in streaming mode with consistent framing. Automatic fallback to standard assistant response occurs when tool is missing or times out.
- Structured output: improve JSON-schema hints via content-type metadata and ensure `format: structured` mode yields a single top-level JSON object (we now post-validate and add a best-effort repair step that attempts to fix common trailing-comma or newline issues).
- Tests: added integration conformance tests against a small OpenAI-spec test corpus (parity cases for roles, stop sequences, logprobs, streaming boundaries, and function calls).

Commits (summary):
- feat(openai-compat): normalize roles and add warning logs for unknown roles
- feat(streaming): implement stop-sequence detector for streaming chunks + unit tests
- feat(logprobs): collect and emit final token logprobs for streamed responses
- feat(functions): streaming tool.call event framing and fallback behavior
- fix(structured-output): add post-emit JSON repair pass and schema validation
- test: add end-to-end ParityConformanceTest and multiple test vectors
- ci: add parity test job to nightly matrix

Files/areas changed (high-level):
- src/api/openai_compat_layer.rs: role normalization, request validation, stop/priority logic
- src/serving/streaming/stream_processor.rs: streaming stop detector, chunk framing changes
- src/serving/logging/logprobs_collector.rs: final logprobs aggregation and payload attach
- src/tools/function_invoker.rs: tool.call event emit + fallback handling
- src/formatters/structured_output.rs: post-emit validation & repair utilities
- tests/conformance/parity_tests.rs: new test vectors and harness
- docs/openai_compat.md: compatibility contract updates and examples

Review conversation (highlights):
- Evan Cheng (reviewer): "Nice consolidation — can you clarify why unknown roles are warnings not errors?"
  - Author reply: "We chose warning to preserve existing third-party SDK behavior where some clients send non-standard roles (e.g., 'bot'). If we error we risk breaking many customers. We'll add a lint to recommend migrating to standard roles and log distinct telemetry."
- Priya Natarajan (reviewer): "Stop handling looks good but how does this impact latency for 2048+ token streams?"
  - Author reply: "Stop detector uses a rolling finite-state-machine over chunks; worst-case per-chunk overhead is O(length_of_chunk * number_of_stop_seqs). We've optimized common-case with a prefix trie and early exit; measured throughput impact <1% in perf-canary tests for large sequences."
- Liam O'Connor: "Are there any backward incompatible changes for SDKs relying on streaming partial logprobs?"
  - Author reply: "We intentionally do not emit partial token logprobs. We document this in openai_compat.md and coordinated with SDK owners. If a customer needs partial logprobs we can add an opt-in flag, but parity with OpenAI was prioritized."
- Follow-up approvals: Evan (approved), Priya (approved after minor test additions), Liam (approved).

CI and testing:
- CI matrix ran: unit, integration, static-analysis, nightly-parity (new job). All jobs passed on final push. One earlier run failed lint due to formatting in structured_output.rs; fixed in subsequent commit. Nightly parity job added to ensure future regressions are caught.

Backward compatibility and migration: 
- Default behavior is backward compatible for most customers. The only behavioral change is stricter post-emit JSON validation in structured-output mode; when we attempt automatic repair that produces a different shape we log a warning and include both raw and repaired payloads in the response metadata for downstream consumers to opt-in.
- SDK owners notified to update examples for logprobs and function-call streaming semantics.

Performance:
- End-to-end perf-canary for streaming throughput shows <2% median latency regression on small messages and <1% on large messages. CPU overhead for stop detection and logprob aggregation is negligible compared to model decode.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated behind 'openai_chat_parity' for 2 weeks with internal dogfooding.
- Gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with parity conformance checks and alerting on increase in 5xx or malformed output rates.

Release notes: "OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility improvements: normalized roles, streaming-aware stop handling, final token logprobs in final payloads, stable function/tool streaming events, and improved structured-output validation and repair. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration guidance and examples."

Notes: linked: ENG-1423 (customer regression), ENG-1589 (parity test harness). This PR is intentionally conservative on breaking changes.
